answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock stake in a cryptographic haven with a quadratic penalty function: registering $N$ identities requires burning stake proportional to $O(N^2)$, achieving superlinear cost scaling. When an identity exhibits malicious coordination, its stake is permanently burned, transforming a cheap attack into an unsustainable expenditure that peaks at an economic zenith. Just as enduring as quartz, this deterministic slashing creates insurmountable mathematical friction that renders large-scale identity replication mathematically unfeasible.
